title: Xiongnu Empire founded
description: Modu Chanyu kills his father and unites the steppe tribes in the first nomadic empire, a rival of Han China for two centuries.

title: Han army defeats the Northern Xiongnu
description: The Han general Dou Xian defeats the Northern Xiongnu and has an inscription cut into a cliff to record the victory.

title: Kul Tigin inscription
description: A memorial stone to the prince Kul Tigin is set up, bearing the oldest long texts in a Turkic language.

title: Uyghur Khaganate founded
description: The Uyghurs overthrow the Turkic khaganate and build a capital city on the Orkhon.

title: Kyrgyz destroy Ordu-Baliq
description: Yenisei Kyrgyz sack the Uyghur capital, and the Uyghurs move south and west into what is now north-western China.

title: Birth of Temüjin
description: The future Genghis Khan is born on the Onon river; the year is uncertain.

title: Genghis Khan proclaimed
description: An assembly of the steppe peoples proclaims Temüjin as Genghis Khan, founding the Mongol Empire.

title: Death of Genghis Khan
description: Genghis Khan dies during the final campaign against the Western Xia, leaving an empire from the Pacific to the Caspian Sea.

title: Karakorum built
description: Ögedei Khan walls the town and builds a palace, making Karakorum the capital of the Mongol Empire.

title: Toluid Civil War
description: Kublai defeats his brother Ariq Böke, who had been elected khan in Mongolia, and the centre of the empire moves to China.

title: Battle of Buir Lake
description: A Ming army destroys the court of the Northern Yuan khan, twenty years after the Mongols were driven from China.

title: Erdene Zuu monastery founded
description: Abtai Sain Khan builds the first Buddhist monastery of Khalkha Mongolia beside the ruins of Karakorum, as Tibetan Buddhism becomes the religion of the Mongols.

title: Zanabazar enthroned
description: The Khalkha nobles recognise the child Zanabazar as their spiritual leader, and his travelling monastery-camp later becomes Ulaanbaatar.

title: Khalkha submit to the Qing
description: After fleeing the Dzungar invasion the Khalkha princes accept the Kangxi Emperor as their ruler, and Mongolia stays under Qing rule until 1911.

title: Battle of Jao Modo
description: A Qing army defeats the Dzungar ruler Galdan, securing Qing control of Khalkha Mongolia.

title: Treaty of Kyakhta
description: Russia and the Qing fix the border between Siberia and Mongolia and open a trading post on it.

title: Urga settles on the Tuul
description: The monastery-town of the Jebtsundamba Khutuktu, which had moved many times, settles at the site of today's capital.

title: Independence declared
description: As the Qing dynasty collapses the Khalkha nobles enthrone the Bogd Khan as ruler of an independent Mongolia.

title: Treaty of Kyakhta
description: Russia, China and Mongolia agree that Outer Mongolia is autonomous under Chinese suzerainty.

title: Ungern-Sternberg takes Urga
description: The White Russian general drives out the Chinese garrison that had occupied the capital since 1919 and restores the Bogd Khan.

title: People's Revolution
description: Mongolian revolutionaries backed by the Red Army set up a new government in the capital, a day kept as the national holiday.

title: Mongolian People's Republic proclaimed
description: After the death of the Bogd Khan a constitution creates the world's second socialist state, and the capital is renamed Ulaanbaatar.

title: Great Repression
description: On Soviet orders the government of Choibalsan kills tens of thousands of people, most of them Buddhist lamas, and destroys nearly all the monasteries.

title: Battles of Khalkhin Gol
description: Soviet and Mongolian forces under Zhukov defeat the Japanese army on the border with Manchukuo, after which Japan turns its expansion southwards.

title: Independence referendum
description: Voters approve independence from China by an official count of 100 per cent, and China recognises it the following January.

title: Democratic Revolution
description: After months of peaceful protests and a hunger strike the Politburo of the ruling party resigns, ending one-party rule.

title: First multi-party election
description: Mongolia holds its first free parliamentary election, which the former ruling party wins.

title: New constitution
description: A democratic constitution comes into force and the country drops the name People's Republic.

title: Democratic Union wins election
description: The opposition coalition defeats the Mongolian People's Revolutionary Party, the first peaceful change of ruling party since 1921.

title: Ulaanbaatar riot
description: Protests over alleged election fraud turn violent, five people are killed and a state of emergency is declared for the first time.
